questions.q: What are the three types of tissue systems on the basis of their structure and location?

questions.q: What are the main components of the epidermal tissue system?
questions.solution: The epidermal tissue system forms the outer-most covering of the whole plant body and comprises epidermal cells, stomata and the epidermal appendages – the trichomes and hairs. The epidermis is the outermost layer of the primary plant body. It is made up of elongated, compactly arranged cells, which form a continuous layer. Epidermis is usually single-Layered. Epidermal cells are parenchymatous with a small amount of cytoplasm lining the cell wall and a large vacuole. The outside of the epidermis is often covered with a waxy thick layer called the cuticle which prevents the loss of water. Cuticle is absent in roots. Stomata are structures present in the epidermis of leaves. Stomata regulate the process of transpiration and gaseous exchange. Each stoma is composed of two bean-shaped cells known as guard cells which enclose stomatal pore. In grasses, the guard cells are dumb-bell shaped. The outer walls of guard cells (away from the stomatal pore) are thin and the inner walls (towards the stomatal pore) are highly thickened. The guard cells possess chloroplasts and regulate the opening and closing of stomata. Sometimes, a few epidermal cells, in the vicinity of the guard cells become specialised in their shape and size and are known as subsidiary cells. The stomatal aperture, guard cells and the surrounding subsidiary cells are together called stomatal apparatus The cells of epidermis bear a number of hairs. The root hairs are unicellular elongations of the epidermal cells and help absorb water and minerals from the soil. On the stem the epidermal hairs are called trichomes. The trichomes in the shoot system are usually multicellular. They may be branched or unbranched and soft or stiff. They may even be secretory. The trichomes help in preventing water loss due to transpiration.

questions.q: What is the outermost layer of a dicot root ?
questions.solution: : The outermost layer is epiblema. Many of the cells of epiblema protrude in the form of unicellular root hairs. The cortex consists of several layers of thin-walled parenchyma cells with intercellular spaces. The innermost layer of the cortex is called endodermis. It comprises a single layer of barrel-shaped cells without any intercellular spaces. The tangential as well as radial walls of the endodermal cells have a deposition of water-impermeable, waxy material suberin in the form of casparian strips. Next to endodermis lies a few layers of thick-walled parenchyomatous cells referred to as pericycle. Initiation of lateral roots and vascular cambium during the secondary growth takes place in these cells. The pith is small or inconspicuous.The parenchymatous cells which lie between the xylem and the phloem are called conjuctive tissue. There are usually two to four xylem and phloem patches. Later, a cambium ring develops between the xylem and phloem. All tissues on the innerside of the endodermis such as pericycle, vascular bundles and pith constitute the stele.

questions.q: What is the outermost protective layer of a leaf?
questions.solution: The vertical section of a dorsiventral leaf through the lamina shows three main parts, namely, epidermis, mesophyll and vascular system. The epidermis which covers both the upper surface (adaxial epidermis) and lower surface (abaxial epidermis) of the leaf has a conspicuous cuticle. The abaxial epidermis generally bears more stomata than the adaxial epidermis. The latter may even lack stomata. The tissue between the upper and the lower epidermis is called the mesophyll. Mesophyll, which possesses chloroplasts and carry out photosynthesis, is made up of parenchyma. It has two types of cells – the palisade parenchyma and the spongy parenchyma. The adaxially placed palisade parenchyma is made up of elongated cells, which are arranged vertically and parallel to each other. The oval or round and loosely arranged spongy parenchyma is situated below the palisade cells and extends to the lower epidermis. There are numerous large spaces and air cavities between these cells. Vascular system includes vascular bundles, which can be seen in the veins and the midrib. The size of the vascular bundles are dependent on the size of the veins. The veins vary in thickness in the reticulate venation of the dicot leaves. The vascular bundles are surrounded by a layer of thick walled bundle sheath cells. and find the position of xylem in the vascular bundle.

options: Subsidiary cells - A few guard cells, in the vicinity of the epidermal cells become specialized in their shape and size and are known as subsidiary cells
Epidermal cells - Epidermal cells are sclerenchymatous with a small amount of cytoplasm lining the cell wall and a large vacuole
Guard cells - The guard cells possess chloroplasts and regulate the opening and closing of stomata
questions.solution: Epidermal cells are parenchymatous with a small amount of cytoplasm lining the cell wall and a large vacuole. The outside of the epidermis is often covered with a waxy thick layer called the cuticle which prevents the loss of water. Cuticle is absent in roots. Stomata are structures present in the epidermis of leaves. Stomata regulate the process of transpiration and gaseous exchange. Each stoma is composed of two bean shaped cells known as guard cells which enclose stomatal pore. In grasses, the guard cells are dumb-bell shaped. The outer walls of guard cells (away from the stomatal pore) are thin and the inner walls (towards the stomatal pore) are highly thickened. The guard cells possess chloroplasts and regulate the opening and closing of stomata. Sometimes, a few epidermal cells, in the vicinity of the guard cells become specialised in their shape and size and are known as subsidiary cells.

4.The cortex of the dicotyledonous stem consists of two sub-zones.
5.The outermost layer of the dicotyledonous stem is the epidermis.
questions.solution: The epidermis is the outermost protective layer of the stem
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1.Vascular bundles in monocot stems are arranged in a ring.
2.The hypodermis in dicot stems is made of parenchymatous cells.
3.The hypodermis in dicot stems is made of collenchymatous cells.

5.The hypodermis in dicot stems is absent.
questions.solution: The outer hypodermis consists of a few layers of collenchymatous cells just below the epidermis,
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1.The cortex of the dicotyledonous stem consists of four sub-zones.
2.The pith in dicot stems is composed of parenchymatous cells.
3.Vascular bundles in dicot stems are scattered.
4.The hypodermis in monocot stems is made of collenchymatous cells.
5.The pith in dicot stems is composed of xylem and phloem.
questions.solution: A large number of rounded, parenchymatous cells with large intercellular spaces which occupy the central portion of the stem constitute the pith,

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1.The hypodermis in dicot stems is made of sclerenchymatous cells
2.Vascular bundles in monocot stems are scattered.
3.The pith in dicot stems is composed of collenchymatous cells.
4.Vascular bundles in monocot stems are absent.
5.bundles in monocot stems are arranged in a circle.
questions.solution: The monocot stem has a sclerenchymatous hypodermis, a large number of scattered vascular bundles
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1.The epidermis covers both the upper and lower surfaces of the leaf.
2.The adaxial epidermis generally has more stomata than the abaxial epidermis.
3.The mesophyll is located between the upper and lower epidermis.
4.The abaxial epidermis may lack stomata.
5.The cuticle is more prominent on the abaxial epidermis.
questions.solution: he epidermis which covers both the upper surface (adaxial epidermis) and lower surface (abaxial epidermis) of the leaf," and that "The tissue between the upper and the lower epidermis is called the mesophyll, the abaxial epidermis generally bears more stomata. the adaxial epidermis may even lack stomata, not the abaxial epidermis.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1.The mesophyll is composed of palisade and spongy parenchyma.
2.The palisade parenchyma is located below the spongy parenchyma.
3.The spongy parenchyma has large spaces and air cavities between cells.
4.The mesophyll carries out photosynthesis.
5.The spongy parenchyma is arranged vertically and parallel to each other.
questions.solution: Mesophyll, which possesses chloroplasts and carry out photosynthesis, is made up of parenchyma. It has two types of cells – the palisade parenchyma and the spongy parenchyma,There are numerous large spaces and air cavities between these cells," the palisade parenchyma is located above the spongy parenchyma, and the palisade parenchyma, not the spongy parenchyma, is arranged vertically.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1.Vascular bundles are present in the veins and midrib of the leaf.
2.The size of vascular bundles depends on the size of the veins.
3.Vascular bundles are surrounded by a layer of thin-walled bundle sheath cells.
4.In dicot leaves, the veins vary in thickness in reticulate venation.
5.Xylem is located in the vascular bundles.
questions.solution: Vascular system includes vascular bundles, which can be seen in the veins and the midrib, "The size of the vascular bundles are dependent on the size of the veins" and that "The veins vary in thickness in the reticulate venation of the dicot leaves, xylem is present in the vascular bundles.the bundle sheath cells are thick-walled, not thin-walled.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1.In isobilateral leaves, stomata are present on both surfaces of the epidermis.
2.The mesophyll in isobilateral leaves is differentiated into palisade and spongy parenchyma.
3.Bulliform cells are present in grasses.
4.Bulliform cells help in minimizing water loss.
5.The anatomy of isobilateral leaves is similar to that of dorsiventral leaves in every way.
questions.solution: In an isobilateral leaf, the stomata are present on both the surfaces of the epidermis, In grasses, certain adaxial epidermal cells along the veins modify themselves into large, empty, colourless cells. These are called bulliform cells," and "When they are flaccid due to water stress, they make the leaves curl inwards to minimize water loss, the mesophyll in isobilateral leaves is not differentiated into palisade and spongy parenchyma. the anatomy of isobilateral leaves is similar in many ways, not every way.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1.Monocot leaves have parallel venation.
2.Vascular bundles in monocot leaves are similar in size.
3.Vascular bundles in monocot leaves are surrounded by thick-walled bundle sheath cells.
4.Bulliform cells are present in dicot leaves.
5.Water-containing cavities are present in the vascular bundles of monocot leaves.
questions.solution: The parallel venation in monocot leaves is reflected in the near similar sizes of vascular bundles, It also mentions that vascular bundles in monocot leaves are surrounded by a sclerenchymatous bundle sheath (which is thick-walled), and that "water-containing cavities are present within the vascular bundles, bulliform cells are mentioned in grasses, not dicot leaves.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Epidermal StructuresDescription
A. Epidermal Cells1. Waxy layer preventing water loss
B. Guard Cells2. Cells regulating transpiration and gas exchange
C. Cuticle3. Unicellular elongations that absorb water and minerals
D. Trichomes4. Parenchymatous cells forming a continuous outer layer
questions.solution: Epidermal cells form a continuous outer layer, guard cells regulate transpiration and gas exchange, the cuticle is a waxy layer preventing water loss, and trichomes are unicellular elongations that absorb water and minerals.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
FeaturesTypes
A. Guard Cells in Grasses1. Dumb-bell shaped
B. Epidermal Cells2. Multicellular, may be branched
C. Root Hairs3. Unicellular elongations
D. Trichomes4. Parenchymatous cells
questions.solution: Guard cells in grasses are dumb-bell shaped, epidermal cells are parenchymatous, root hairs are unicellular elongations, and trichomes are multicellular and may be branched.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Epidermal ComponentsFunctions
A. Stomata1. Prevents water loss
B. Cuticle2. Regulate transpiration and gas exchange
C. Trichomes3. Prevent water loss due to transpiration
D. Guard Cells4. Allow gas exchange
questions.solution: Stomata allow gas exchange, cuticle prevents water loss, trichomes help prevent water loss due to transpiration, and guard cells regulate transpiration and gas exchange
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Ground Tissue TypesLocation
A. Parenchyma1. Cortex, pericycle, pith, medullary rays
B. Collenchyma2. Leaves, thin-walled, chloroplast-containing cells
C. Sclerenchyma3. Supporting tissue in stems and leaves
D. Mesophyll4. Hard, supportive tissue
questions.solution: Parenchyma is found in the cortex, pericycle, pith, and medullary rays, collenchyma provides support in stems and leaves, sclerenchyma is hard and supportive, and mesophyll is in leaves and contains chloroplasts
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Stomatal Apparatus FeaturesStomatal Types
A. Guard Cells with Chloroplasts1. Structures surrounding the stomatal pore
B. Stomatal Aperture2. Allows gas exchange
C. Subsidiary Cells3. Regulates the opening and closing of stomata
D. Stomatal Pore4. Cells that assist guard cells
questions.solution: Guard cells with chloroplasts regulate the opening and closing of stomata, the stomatal aperture allows gas exchange, subsidiary cells assist guard cells, and the stomatal pore is surrounded by structures that control gas exchange
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Epidermal AppendagesTypes
A. Root Hairs1. Unicellular elongations
B. Trichomes2. Waxy layer on the surface
C. Cuticle3. Multicellular, branched or unbranched
D. Guard Cells4. Specialized cells regulating transpiration
questions.solution: Root hairs are unicellular elongations, trichomes are multicellular and may be branched or unbranched, cuticle is a waxy layer, and guard cells are specialized for regulating transpiration.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Vascular BundlesDescription
A. Open Vascular Bundles1. No cambium present, do not form secondary tissues
B. Closed Vascular Bundles2. Xylem and phloem arranged in an alternate manner
C. Radial Vascular Bundles3. Xylem and phloem are jointly situated along the same radius
D. Conjoint Vascular Bundles4. Cambium present between xylem and phloem, forms secondary tissues
questions.solution: Open vascular bundles have cambium present and can form secondary tissues. Closed vascular bundles have no cambium and do not form secondary tissues. Radial vascular bundles have xylem and phloem arranged alternately. Conjoint vascular bundles have xylem and phloem jointly situated along the same radius.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Components of dicot rootFunctions
A. Epiblema1. Initiates lateral roots and vascular cambium
B. Cortex2. Outermost layer with unicellular root hairs
C. Endodermis3. Thin-walled parenchyma cells, contains casparian strips
D. Pericycle4. Several layers of thin-walled parenchyma cells
questions.solution: Epiblema is the outermost layer with root hairs, cortex consists of thin-walled parenchyma cells, endodermis has casparian strips, and pericycle initiates lateral roots and vascular cambium.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
TermsCharacteristics
A. Cambium1. Tissue between xylem and phloem
B. Conjunctive Tissue2. Tissue responsible for water and nutrient transport
C. Xylem3. Present between xylem and phloem in dicotyledonous plants
D. Phloem4. Tissue involved in the transport of food
questions.solution: Cambium is present between xylem and phloem in dicotyledonous plants. Conjunctive tissue is located between xylem and phloem. Xylem transports water and nutrients, while phloem transports food.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Vascular Bundle TypesExamples
A. Radial Vascular Bundles1. Sunflower root
B. Conjoint Open Vascular Bundles2. Monocot stems
C. Conjoint Closed Vascular Bundles3. Common in stems and leaves
D. Dicotyledonous Vascular Bundles4. Roots
questions.solution: Radial vascular bundles are found in roots. Conjoint open vascular bundles are not specifically given as examples but typically occur in dicot stems. Conjoint closed vascular bundles are found in monocot stems, and dicotyledonous vascular bundles are common in stems and leaves.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Stem LayersDescriptions
A. Epidermis1. Provides mechanical strength and consists of collenchymatous cells
B. Hypodermis2. Outermost protective layer covered with a thin cuticle
C. Endodermis3. Rich in starch grains and referred to as the starch sheath
D. Pericycle4. Present on the inner side of the endodermis and above the phloem
questions.solution: The epidermis is the outermost protective layer, the hypodermis provides mechanical strength, the endodermis is rich in starch grains, and the pericycle is present above the phloem.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Vascular Bundle CharacteristicsFeatures
A. Conjoint1. Contains both xylem and phloem together
B. Open2. Xylem development starts from the center and matures outward
C. Endarch Protoxylem3. Characterized by the arrangement of xylem and phloem in the same radius
D. Medullary Rays4. Radially placed parenchymatous cells between vascular bundles
questions.solution: Conjoint bundles have both xylem and phloem together, open bundles have cambium, endarch protoxylem has xylem development from the center, and medullary rays are radially placed cells.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Stem ComponentsTypes of Cells/Tissues
A. Hypodermis1. Collenchymatous cells
B. Cortical Layers2. Parenchymatous cells with intercellular spaces
C. Pericycle3. Parenchymatous cells with large intercellular spaces in the center
D. Pith4. Sclerenchymatous cells in semi-lunar patches
questions.solution: Hypodermis has collenchymatous cells, cortical layers are parenchymatous with intercellular spaces, pericycle contains sclerenchymatous cells, and pith has large intercellular spaces.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Component of moncot stemCharacteristics
A. Hypodermis1. Sclerenchymatous in nature
B. Vascular Bundles2. Scattered and surrounded by sclerenchymatous tissue
C. Bundle Sheath3. Large and conspicuous parenchymatous tissue
D. Ground Tissue4. Conjoint and closed
questions.solution: The hypodermis is sclerenchymatous, vascular bundles are conjoint and closed, each bundle is surrounded by a sclerenchymatous bundle sheath, and the ground tissue is large and parenchymatous
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
FeaturesTypes
A. Conjoint1. Surrounded by sclerenchymatous sheath
B. Closed2. Do not have cambium
C. Peripheral Bundles3. Generally larger in size
D. Centrally Located Bundles4. Arranged in a scattered manner
questions.solution: Conjoint bundles are scattered, closed bundles lack cambium, peripheral bundles are smaller, and centrally located bundles are larger.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Tissue TypesDescriptions
A. Sclerenchyma1. Scattered throughout the stem
B. Parenchyma2. Large, conspicuous, and present in the ground tissue
C. Vascular Bundles3. Absent in the phloem but present within bundles
D. Water-Containing Cavities4. Surrounds vascular bundles and provides support
questions.solution: Sclerenchyma surrounds vascular bundles, parenchyma is large and present in ground tissue, vascular bundles are scattered, and water-containing cavities are present within bundles.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
TermsDescriptions
A. Bundle Sheath1. Scattered and surrounded by sclerenchymatous sheath
B. Ground Tissue2. Large and conspicuous parenchymatous tissue
C. Vascular Bundle Arrangement3. Absent in the phloem, present within bundles
D. Water-Containing Cavities4. Peripheral bundles are smaller than central ones
questions.solution: The bundle sheath surrounds the vascular bundles, ground tissue is large and parenchymatous, vascular bundle arrangement shows smaller peripheral bundles, and water-containing cavities are present within bundles.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Vascular Bundle TypesOccurrence
A. Conjoint1. Found in dicotyledonous stems with cambium
B. Open2. Found in monocotyledons without cambium
C. Closed3. Xylem and phloem together on the same radius
D. Radial4. Xylem and phloem arranged alternately
questions.solution: Conjoint bundles have xylem and phloem together, open bundles have cambium, closed bundles lack cambium, and radial bundles have xylem and phloem arranged alternately
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Cortex LayersCharacteristics
A. Hypodermis1. Rounded thin-walled cells with intercellular spaces
B. Cortical Layers below Hypodermis2. Collenchymatous cells providing mechanical strength
C. Endodermis3. Rich in starch grains and known as starch sheath
D. Medullary Rays4. Radially placed parenchymatous cells between vascular bundles
questions.solution: Hypodermis has collenchymatous cells, cortical layers below it are rounded parenchymatous cells, endodermis is rich in starch grains, and medullary rays are radially placed parenchymatous cells.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
TermsStructures
A. Cuticle1. Outermost protective layer covering the epidermis
B. Trichomes2. Hair-like structures on the epidermis
C. Stomata3. Parenchymatous cells between vascular bundles
D. Medullary Rays4. Pores in the epidermis for gas exchange
questions.solution: The cuticle is the protective layer on the epidermis, trichomes are hair-like structures, stomata are pores for gas exchange, and medullary rays are parenchymatous cells between vascular bundles.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Epidermis TypesCharacteristics
A. Adaxial Epidermis1. Generally bears more stomata
B. Abaxial Epidermis2. May lack stomata and covered with cuticle
C. Hypodermis3. Provides mechanical strength to the stem
D. Cuticle4. Outermost protective layer of the leaf
questions.solution: The adaxial epidermis may lack stomata, the abaxial epidermis generally bears more stomata, the hypodermis provides mechanical strength, and the cuticle is the outermost protective layer.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Mesophyll ComponentsDescriptions
A. Palisade Parenchyma1. Surrounding vascular bundles
B. Spongy Parenchyma2. Oval or round cells with large intercellular spaces
C. Epidermal Cells3. Cells covering the leaf surface
D. Bundle Sheath Cells4. Elongated cells arranged vertically
questions.solution: The palisade parenchyma consists of elongated cells arranged vertically, the spongy parenchyma has oval or round cells with large intercellular spaces, epidermal cells cover the leaf surface, and bundle sheath cells surround vascular bundles.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Vascular Bundle CharacteristicsDescriptions
A. Vascular Bundle Size1. Dependent on the size of veins
B. Vascular Bundle Arrangement2. Surrounded by thick-walled cells
C. Bundle Sheath Cells3. Vary in thickness in reticulate venation
D. Vascular Bundle Type4. Conjoint, open, and with endarch protoxylem
questions.solution: The size of vascular bundles depends on the size of veins, their arrangement varies in thickness with reticulate venation, they are surrounded by thick-walled bundle sheath cells, and they are conjoint, open, and with endarch protoxylem.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Leaf TypesFeatures
A. Dorsiventral Leaf1. Stomata present on both surfaces
B. Isobilateral Leaf2. Mesophyll differentiated into palisade and spongy parenchyma
C. Monocot Leaf3. Stomata only on the lower surface
D. Bulliform Leaf4. Leaf structure with parallel venation
questions.solution: The dorsiventral leaf has mesophyll differentiated into palisade and spongy parenchyma, the isobilateral leaf has stomata on both surfaces, the monocot leaf has parallel venation, and bulliform leaves have stomata only on the lower surface.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Cell ModificationsFunctions
A. Bulliform Cells1. Absorb water and help the leaf curl inwards when flaccid
B. Epidermal Cells2. Provide mechanical strength to the stem
C. Sclerenchyma Cells3. Protects the leaf and aids in structural support
D. Collenchyma Cells4. Contribute to water transport and storage
questions.solution: Bulliform cells help the leaf curl inwards when flaccid, epidermal cells protect the leaf, sclerenchyma cells provide mechanical strength, and collenchyma cells contribute to structural support.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Venation TypesCharacteristics
A. Parallel Venation1. Vascular bundles are nearly similar in size
B. Reticulate Venation2. Vascular bundles vary in thickness
C. Isobilateral Venation3. Mesophyll is differentiated into palisade and spongy parenchyma
D. Dorsiventral Venation4. Stomata are present on both surfaces
questions.solution: Parallel venation has vascular bundles nearly similar in size, reticulate venation varies in thickness, isobilateral venation has stomata on both surfaces, and dorsiventral venation has differentiated mesophyll.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Leaf TissuesLocations
A. Adaxial Epidermis1. Contains palisade and spongy parenchyma
B. Mesophyll2. Typically has more stomata
C. Abaxial Epidermis3. Covers the upper leaf surface
D. Vascular Bundles4. Found in veins and midrib
questions.solution: The adaxial epidermis covers the upper surface, mesophyll contains palisade and spongy parenchyma, the abaxial epidermis typically has more stomata, and vascular bundles are found in veins and the midrib
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Leaf AdaptationsLeaf Types
A. Bulliform Cells1. Characteristic of dicot leave
B. Stomata on Both Surfaces2. Characteristic of isobilateral leaves
C. Parallel Venation3. Reflects the parallel arrangement of veins
D. Reticulate Venation4. Found in grasses
questions.solution: Bulliform cells are found in grasses, stomata on both surfaces is characteristic of isobilateral leaves, parallel venation reflects parallel vein arrangement, and reticulate venation is characteristic of dicot leaves.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
ComponentDescriptions
A. Vascular Bundles1.Present on both surfaces of the epidermis
B. Parallel Venation2. Similar in size across the leaf
C. Isobilateral Leaf3. Large, colorless cells that help in water conservation
D. Bulliform Cells4. Reflects the parallel arrangement of veins
questions.solution: Vascular bundles in monocot leaves are similar in size, parallel venation reflects the parallel vein arrangement, isobilateral leaf has stomata on both surfaces, and bulliform cells are large and colorless, aiding in water conservation.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Types of Mesophyll CellsFeatures
A. Palisade Parenchyma1. Elongated cells arranged adaxially
B. Spongy Parenchyma2. Possesses chlorophyll for photosynthesis
C. Mesophyll3. Present between the upper and lower epidermis
D. Chloroplasts4. Carries out photosynthesis
questions.solution: Palisade parenchyma consists of elongated cells arranged adaxially.Spongy parenchyma carries out photosynthesis.Mesophyll is located between the upper and lower epidermis.Chloroplasts possess chlorophyll for photosynthesis.

to know when the plant will die
to know about the internal structures which show adaptations to diverse environment

questions.solution: In grasses, certain adaxial epidermal cells along the veins modify themselves into large, empty, colourless cells. These are called bulliform cells or motor cells. Bulliform cells help in folding and unfolding of grass leaves.

questions.q: What are the cells that make the leaves curl in plants during water stress?
